Overview ¶

    Package backoff implements jittered exponential delays for retrying operations that fail in transient ways, such as network calls, lock acquisition, or rate-limited APIs.

    A Policy describes the initial delay, the multiplier, the maximum delay, and the amount of random jitter. Policies are plain values, so they can be shared between goroutines and stored in configuration structs without any locking.

    The zero Policy is not useful on its own. Use Default for a reasonable starting point, which begins at 100 milliseconds, doubles on every attempt, and caps the delay at 30 seconds.

    p := backoff.Default
for attempt := 0; ; attempt++ {
	if err := call(); err == nil {
		break
	}
	time.Sleep(p.Delay(attempt))
}

    func Retry

    func Retry(ctx context.Context, p Policy, fn func() error) error

    Retry calls fn until it returns nil, the context is cancelled, or the policy gives up. It returns the last error from fn, wrapped so that errors.Is still matches the original value.
